records.people: Faisal Wisam al-Heims (Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq, appointed March 2023)
records.move: from Director-General of the Trade Bank of Iraq to Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of Iraq
records.summary: Shafaq News reported on 14 March 2023 that the CBI governor appointed Faisal Wisam al-Heims as deputy governor, and that he had been Director-General of the Trade Bank of Iraq, which the report describes as a state-owned bank; it also says he chaired the Iraq Securities Commission. Neither side of this career is private finance: the Trade Bank of Iraq is stated to be state-owned and the Securities Commission is a regulator, so this is a public-sector move.

records.people: Dasho Penjore (Royal Monetary Authority Deputy Managing Director 2003-2006; Governor from December 2015)
records.move: from Deputy Managing Director of the Royal Monetary Authority, via Chief Chamberlain to the King and Chief Executive Officer of the National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan, to Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority
records.summary: The Financial Institutions Training Institute biography says Penjore began his career at the Royal Monetary Authority in 1987, served as its Deputy Managing Director from 2003 to 2006, was appointed Chief Chamberlain to the King in 2006, was Chief Executive Officer of the National Pension & Provident Fund of Bhutan, and was appointed RMA Governor in December 2015. The National Pension & Provident Fund is a statutory pension body, so no side of this career is private finance; this is a public-sector move.

records.people: Addis Ababa Othow (Bank of South Sudan division head from 2010; First Deputy Governor 2022-2023 and from February 2025; Governor from June 2025)
records.move: from head of the Bank of South Sudan's non-banking division to General Manager of Operations at Equity Bank in Nairobi (2015) and Managing Director of Equity Bank South Sudan Ltd (2018), then First Deputy Governor of the Bank of South Sudan (2022), briefly back to Equity Bank after October 2023, and Governor from June 2025
records.summary: Eye Radio's profile gives a dated career: he joined the Central Bank of Sudan as a banking inspector in 1997, joined Ivory Bank in 1998, joined the Bank of South Sudan in 2010 as head of its non-banking division and in 2013 headed its Planning, Regulation and Licensing Division, then in 2015 joined Equity Bank's Nairobi headquarters as General Manager of Operations, becoming Managing Director of Equity Bank South Sudan Ltd in 2018. The article says that in moving to Equity Bank he moved back to the private sector, and he was First Deputy Governor from 2022 to October 2023, returned briefly to Equity Bank, was reappointed First Deputy Governor in February 2025 and appointed Governor in June 2025.
records.source_title: Meet Dr Othow, South Sudan's new central bank governor (Eye Radio)

records.people: Mohamed Khair Ahmed Al-Zubair (Governor of the Central Bank of Sudan from March 2011)
records.move: from Vice President of the Bank of Sahel and Sahara Community (2002-2009) to Governor of the Central Bank of Sudan, having earlier been Minister of Finance and National Economy (2000-2001) and president of the board of the Saudi Sudanese Bank
records.summary: The Central Bank of Sudan's own biography page gives a dated career: Vice President of the Bank of Sahel and Sahara Community from 2002 to 2009, Minister of Finance and National Economy 2000-2001, state minister and planning posts in the finance ministry through the 1980s and 1990s, and Governor of the Central Bank of Sudan from March 2011. It also lists former board seats at the Saudi Sudanese Bank (president of the board), the Financial Investment Bank and the Agricultural Bank of Sudan, without dates. No source opened states the ownership of any of those banks, and the dated employers immediately either side of the governorship are an intergovernmental bank and a finance ministry, so the career as stated is a public-sector one.

records.people: Yussur A. F. Abrar (Governor of the Central Bank of Somalia, 2013)

The report names none of the international banks and gives no dates, and no source opened states the ownership of TLG Financial Services, so the record is flagged for an ownership check.
